United States tops the list of the most dangerous countries for women in childbirth, according to the World Health Organisation, a situation which has left millions in danger of dying in childbirth.
The report, compiled by the UK-based charity Maternal Health Alliance, reveals that one in four women die in childbirth worldwide, and for American women, the risk is particularly high.
The US has the highest maternal mortality rates in the world, with women dying from pregnancy-related causes more than five times as often as men, despite the same number of pregnancies.
The figures are particularly alarming as the country is home to the highest fertility rate of any developed nation.
Why are American woman dying in childbirth, and how can the problem be solved?
The WHO, which was established by the UN in 1948, has compiled a report on maternal mortality rates, which show that America has the highest rate in the world - with one in four deaths linked to childbirth.

For years, the trucking business has been an industry rife with environmental concerns. Now, a small, independent startup company is changing that.
Move Systems has developed a platform that allows food trucks to convert to an entirely new set of operating requirements. The company's app allows food vendors to buy electricity from nearby solar panels or even to buy their own. Food vendors can then install their own solar panels or electric vehicles.
The move to clean, renewable energy is a far cry from what the food trucks of yore had. Many were run on diesel, and their heaters and electric motors created an immense amount of exhaust.
"This is a shift in the entire industry," said Michael Gorman, CEO of Move Systems. "People are willing to do whatever it takes to do something better for their customers and for the environment."

The first of these planets to be confirmed for life, Kepler-452b, orbits a star in the constellation of Canis Major, the Lion. The planet, located 2,500 light-years away from Earth, orbits its star at a distance of roughly five times the distance between Earth and the sun.

At this distance, Kepler-453b is an ideal laboratory for studying habitability. It lies within the habitable zone of its star, which is an area that a rocky planet can survive in with the right amount of heat and water. The distance to its star is around seven times larger than that of Earth, and the star is located at a distance much greater than Mars.
